assertionResults.reason: With the broker/web URL pointed at an unreachable local address, repo-bound session list/start/stop, status --project, project owner show, and tickets create/list all succeeded from the CLI in an isolated temp repo. The broker-owned `hack auth login` flow alone failed closed with explicit `/v1/auth/session/start` availability guidance.

Offline repo-bound `hack env` flows remained local-first: plaintext writes stayed in `.hack/.env`, secret writes used the configured encrypted_file backend, `env list --show-secrets --json` reported `trust_model: local_only` plus `portable_state.status: not_configured`, and default JSON output still redacted the secret. The dead broker URL therefore did not make env management web-only, while shared/broker state stayed explicitly distinguished instead of implied.

frictions.description: Inside the parent tmux shell, `hack session list` initially targeted the shared tmux server instead of an isolated validator session namespace.
frictions.resolution: Unset `TMUX` for the validation commands and pinned `TMUX_TMPDIR=<tmp>/tmux`, which made `session list/start/stop` operate only on the isolated workspace set.

frictions.description: When `HACK_GLOBAL_CONFIG_PATH` is set, the CLI reads `projects.json` from the config directory rather than from `HOME/.hack`, which is easy to miss during isolated session/status validation.
frictions.resolution: Wrote the temp project registry to `<tmp>/cli-state/projects.json` next to `<tmp>/cli-state/global-config.json` so `session start` and `status --project` resolved the temp repo correctly.

commands.observation: Connection failed as expected, confirming the simulated broker/web outage surface was unreachable.
